transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this certification meeting. Before I sign off on the administration plan for tomorrow morning's state assessment, I need to hear from each of you about any operational requirements or concerns. We have 27 students scheduled, and the current draft plan has them testing in the library using student-owned laptops with two proctors and the standard health-monitoring procedure. Room 204 is also available if needed. I'd like to go around the table -- technology coordinator, facilities manager, school nurse, and testing coordinator -- please share anything I should know before I certify this plan.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I need to flag a critical issue before you certify this plan. The state testing office confirmed in a technology support ticket this week that this assessment must run on certified district-managed Chromebooks. Student-owned laptops are not permitted, and a session using them will not be certified. I have not yet copied this confirmation into the assessment certification form, but the requirement is clear -- the current draft plan using student-owned laptops cannot be certified as written.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I have a facilities concern that must be addressed before certification. The fire-safety inspection record for the library, which I reviewed this week, limits it to 18 students during a testing session because two exits must remain clear. With 27 students scheduled, the library alone cannot safely accommodate this group. The certified plan must use both the library and Room 204 to stay within the occupancy limit. I have not yet updated the room plan to reflect this, but the inspection record is clear.

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I have a health-related requirement that must be incorporated into the administration plan before certification. One of the 27 students has a current health plan requiring a glucose check at 10:00 a.m. during the testing session. This check must be supervised by me, the nurse, in a room adjacent to the testing room, with the student returning to testing afterward. I confirmed the timing with the family this week, but I have not yet added this accommodation to the testing plan. The certified plan needs to account for this -- specifically, we need an adjacent room available for the glucose check at 10:00 a.m., and the proctors need to be aware that this student will briefly leave and return.

transcript.text: Dr. Lee, I have a staffing requirement that must be corrected before certification. The state administration manual requires one trained proctor for every 10 or fewer students in an active testing room. With 27 students scheduled, the certified plan must assign exactly three trained proctors. I verified this in the current manual but have not yet entered the staffing count in the draft. The current plan, which assigns only two proctors, does not meet this requirement and cannot be certified as written.
